title: Work in Progress Is Not Revenue: The Number Most Engineering and Architecture Firms Never Watch
linkedin:
World Town Planning Day is today, a nod to the planners, engineers and architects shaping how our cities grow.

But the sharper commercial story for engineering and architecture firms rarely sits in the pipeline. It sits in a number most practices never watch closely: work in progress.

WIP is design and engineering work a firm has already completed but has not yet invoiced. A project moves through concept design, DA support, documentation and construction phase services, each with a notional billing milestone attached, but the trigger to actually raise that invoice is rarely automatic. It waits on a director's review, a client sign off, or a quiet week to catch up on admin.

Scope variations make it worse. A client asks for a change midway through documentation, the team absorbs the extra hours to keep momentum, and the variation gets logged for billing later. Later rarely arrives on schedule.

A firm can look genuinely profitable on paper and still be short on cash, because the P&L recognises work as it is delivered, not as it is paid for. The firms that manage this well treat invoicing as a stage of delivery, not an admin task, tying milestones to a specific observable trigger and billing variations in the same cycle they occur.

A full pipeline and a growing WIP balance can look identical from the outside. The difference only shows up in the bank account.
